content: 1. Pharmacodynamic synergism between certain drugs can increase the risk of upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets, which may contribute to this risk. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 2. Sulfasalazine increases anticoagulation effects, while mistletoe decreases them. The exact effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Moexipril and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through mechanisms such as renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Momelotinib, a breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions.
